title: Hazel and the Signal
premise: Beatrix Montrose, a disgraced navigator hiding aboard the freighter Hazel, keeps a private log of Meridian Colony's slow suffocation — a war the Core worlds pretend isn't happening. When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the whole system, Beatrix realizes it was a signal: a countdown broadcast through spacetime itself, and only someone with his illegal memory-backup implants can decode it. The backups sleeping in the hold aren't cargo; they're archived minds of dead colonists who recorded the truth about who started the war. To deliver that message to the armada massing at the system's edge, Beatrix must wake them, survive the Core agents hunting the ship, and sacrifice his own stored memories as the transmission key. In the end he sends the truth and shatters the war's justification — but loses every backup of himself except the one still breathing.
about_author: Hazel Ravensworth is the pen name of a former merchant-marine radio operator who spent eleven years on deep-haul routes before turning to fiction. Their work blends hard-science rigor with elegiac character studies of people the future forgot to count.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. During a routine supply run over dying Meridian Colony, gravity fails for exactly nine seconds; instruments record an impossible pattern in the fluctuation. Beatrix hides the data from his crewmates, terrified it will draw attention. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Hold Full of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He descends into the sealed hold where forty-one memory backups — legally contraband, morally unburied dead — hum in cold storage. Through flashbacks we learn he smuggled them out of Meridian before the blockade. Beat: guilt made physical.

chapters.title: Log Entries, Year Four
chapters.summary: Epistolary chapter alternating Beatrix's private logs with colony transmissions. We see Meridian's slow starvation and the Core's official silence. Crewmate Ilsa Voss nearly catches him recording. Beat: loneliness of witness.

chapters.title: Gravity Has a Grammar
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Decoding the nine-second pattern, he finds structure — repetition, variation, intent. It repeats every 61 hours, slightly changed each time. Someone or something is speaking. Beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Ilsa Asks Too Many Questions
chapters.summary: Ilsa Voss's POV. The engineer has noticed power draws toward the hold and Beatrix's night visits. Her suspicion is layered over her own secret: she lost family on Meridian. Beat: mistrust shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: The First Voice
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He interfaces illegally with one backup — Dr. Amara Sen, colony xenolinguist — and her archived memories reveal the gravitational signal matches experiments Meridian conducted before the war. Beat: the past opening like a wound.

chapters.title: Core Ship at the Edge
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. A Directorate cruiser enters the system demanding 'customs inspection' of all traffic. Captain Okafor orders the Hazel dark behind a moon. Beat: the noose tightening.

chapters.title: What Amara Knew
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV inside Amara's memories. Meridian didn't build a weapon; they built a listener, and what it heard from deep space was co-opted by both sides as a war pretext. Beat: revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Directorate officers board under pretense; Ilsa covers for Beatrix, lying smoothly for the first time in her life. They pass inspection by minutes. Beat: complicity forging reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Sixty-One Hours
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The next signal pulse arrives stronger — and addressed, he realizes, in coordinates matching the Hazel itself. The sender knows the backups are here. Beat: hunted by the message itself.

chapters.title: Okafor's Bargain
chapters.summary: Captain Okafor's POV. She reveals she's known about the hold for two years; her silence was bought with the promise of delivery 'when it mattered.' Now the Core offers her amnesty to surrender the cargo. Beat: loyalty priced and weighed.

chapters.title: Waking the Dead
chapters.summary: Beatrix and Ilsa's alternating POV. They begin waking backups temporarily to testify — colonists, soldiers, a Directorate defector — assembling the true record. Each waking costs power they don't have. Beat: found family assembled from ghosts.

chapters.title: The Defector's Warning
chapters.summary: The woken defector, Commander Reyes, warns that the armada at the edge isn't waiting for orders — it's waiting for a trigger, and the gravitational signal may be it. Beat: countdown made explicit.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Airlock
chapters.summary: A crewmate sells their position to the Directorate for passage home. Boarding torpedoes breach the outer hull; Ilsa is gravely injured sealing the hold. Beat: trust broken, cost made blood-real.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. With engines crippled, he navigates the Hazel through Meridian's debris field using memory alone — the route he flew the night he stole the backups. Beat: mastery and penance in one maneuver.

chapters.title: Meridian Below
chapters.summary: Beatrix lands among the colony ruins to repair the antenna array. Walking the streets he once evacuated, he meets survivors the records said were dead. Beat: grief interrupted by grace.

chapters.title: The Message Assembled
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The woken backups finish the testimony: full proof the war's casus belli was fabricated from Meridian's intercepted signal. But playback requires a living neural key — someone implanted like Beatrix. Beat: the price named aloud.

chapters.title: Armada
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The fleet at the edge begins final positioning; a first strike launches toward Meridian's ruins. Hours remain. Beat: inevitability accelerating.

chapters.title: The Key
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He understands: transmitting will burn out his implants and every stored copy of his own mind — his backups are the cipher. He says goodbye to the sleepers, to Ilsa, to the log. Beat: acceptance.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, Beatrix's POV. From Meridian's array, he transmits the testimony through the gravitational channel itself, letting the enemy's own listening network carry the truth to every ship at once. Pain, whiteout, silence. Beat: sacrifice as signal.

chapters.title: Ceasefire Over Ruins
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Fleet weapons go cold mid-approach; Directorate channels flood with the broadcast. Ilsa wakes in the medbay to news of ceasefire talks — and Beatrix alive but stripped of every backup, remembering nothing of the hold. Beat: survival without triumph.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Signal
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, final log entry. He re-reads his own earlier logs like a stranger's diary, learning who he was. The colonists come aboard; the sleepers' backups are returned home to be honored. He chooses to keep flying. Beat: memory lost, family found.
